newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close 2.27 pct lower on electronics.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close 2.27 pct lower on electronics.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower in extremely volatile trade on Thursday, shaken by hectic profit-taking in the electronics sector that defied government efforts to lift the index, brokers said.
The weighted index ended a roller-coaster session by closing 185.52 points or 2.27 percent lower at 7,996.10.
Turnover was a brisk T$120.34 billion.
The downturn furthered a week of huge volatility.

The index plunged more than four percent on Monday and Tuesday on worries linked to an unfolding political row over a spate of unsolved murders, only to mount a sharp 2.89 percent rebound on Wednesday. Brokers said uncertainty remained.
"As long as political instability still is a worry, the index cannot see a sustainable rise," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.
Thursday's session coincided with an annual news conference by President Lee Teng-hui during in Lee apologised for a crime wave that has undermined public confidence in the government.
Brokers said the government had tried to boost the index on Thursday by buying up shares in the heavily weighted financial sector through state-backed funds.

The intervention appeared to have staved off greater losses but could not overcome massive selling in electronics, which tumbled by 5.96 percent on profit-taking and recent price softening for key electronic products and components -- many of which are made in huge numbers in Taiwan.
"The government buying concentrated on big-capital financial shares, but it did not improve general sentiment," said Joe Chiou, an analyst at Taiwan Securities Investment.
